transcript.content: Hi, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?

Um... well, I guess it's mostly work stuff. They changed our setup recently, and... it's just made things a bit difficult. 

I just... I have a hard time sitting idle. I feel like I'm always moving from one thing to the next, and... well, the new work setup just makes that a lot harder to hide now.
Have you ever had a period where you felt unusually high, energized, or euphoric compared with your normal self?
Uh, no. I don't... I don't think so. I wouldn't really use a word like euphoric. Just... just the restlessness I mentioned before. That's about it.
Do you get unwanted thoughts that keep popping into your mind even when you try to ignore them?
Um, no. Not really. I just... no, I don't think I have anything like that. Just regular thoughts, I guess.
Did you have this same kind of restlessness when you were a child?

I suppose so, yeah. It's... well, it's been around a lot longer than this recent job change. 

If I look back at grade school... I remember my teachers usually wrote that I was bright, but careless. Said I talked out of turn a lot. They were always having to remind me to just... stay with my work. So... yeah. I guess it's not new.
Do you often make careless mistakes or miss details when you’re doing work tasks?

Yeah, I suppose. Sometimes. I mean... I'll think I've finished a customer ticket, but... later I'll notice I typed the wrong account number. Or maybe I skipped a required box. Just... missing one little instruction, and the whole thing comes back to me. So, yeah, that happens.
Do you often find yourself worrying a lot about different parts of your life, even when there isn’t a clear reason to?
No... not really. I mean, I don't just sit around worrying for no reason. Just... the usual things, I guess. Nothing out of the ordinary.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient describes a longstanding pattern since childhood of restlessness/hyperactivity and inattentive symptoms, including difficulty sitting still, talking out of turn in school, needing reminders to stay on task, and making careless mistakes at work. Symptoms are causing occupational difficulty, especially after a workplace setup change. Mania, obsessive symptoms, and generalized anxiety were specifically not supported in the interview, making ADHD, predominantly inattentive type/hyperkinetic disorder the best fit among the provided candidates.
